title: Getting a link onto another screen
intro: The end result was a new browser tab. Behind it were a Windows Phone app, a Chrome extension, a web API and Google Cloud Messaging.
paragraphs: SendToChrome dates from 2015. It paired a Windows Phone with a named Chrome browser, using a short code to connect the two.
The phone requested that code from the API. You entered it in the Chrome extension and gave the browser a name. The phone could then list its paired browsers and send a URL to one of them.
The API routed the URL through Google Cloud Messaging. The extension received the message and opened a tab. The phone never needed a direct connection to the desktop.
